title: Reynolds v. Pee Dee Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order because it was not timely filed under BCO 43-2 and dismissed it. It expressly declined to decide whether Mrs. Reynolds could bring a personal-offense charge as an injured party under BCO 31-5 or whether the Session had jurisdiction over claims outside the confession it received.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Kappie Reynolds's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery because it was untimely under BCO 43-2, since it challenged a Session's confession-related action taken more than six months before filing. The ruling did not decide whether Reynolds could bring an injured-party charge or whether the Session had jurisdiction over the confession.
summary: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Kappie Reynolds's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery as judicially out of order. The complaint challenged a Session's reception of and action on a confession at a meeting more than six months before filing, far outside BCO 43-2's sixty-day period; the SJC held the untimeliness was not demonstrated curable. The ruling expressly reserved whether Reynolds could proceed as an injured party under BCO 31-5 and whether the Session had jurisdiction over claims outside the received confession.

evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 19–23 state that the complaint sought to redress acts or decisions of a Session that received and acted upon a confession at a meeting more than six months before the complaint was filed, placing it outside BCO 43-2's sixty-day period.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 19–25 hold the complaint not demonstrated timely and not curable, declare it judicially out of order, and direct dismissal. No merits ruling is made.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Line 27 expressly reserves opinion on whether Mrs. Reynolds can proceed as an injured party under BCO 31-5 or whether the Session had jurisdiction over claims outside the received confession. Line 31 records Donahoe's dissent; line 36 records Ross's recusal for personal advice and prior knowledge.
